hypothesis: The HIP-3 index supervisor must treat only the typed journal/status/cursor mixed-publication interval as bounded degradation rather than fatal process corruption, while retaining a hard fault for persistent incoherence and all other health failures.
decision: Retain the bounded recovery repair. The 05:00 mixed-publication fault was directly observed, deterministic RED tests reproduced it, 6909 non-network tests passed, and the repaired supervisor stayed ready through the real 05:15 boundary while live SP500 readiness recovered. No live backend, strategy, exit, sizing, leverage, or risk change is supported or required.
falsifier: Reject or revise the repair if another transient mixed publication kills the supervisor, persistent incoherence does not hard-fault within the bound, any incoherent evidence authorizes an intent, or cursor, journal, identity, protection, backend, or TUI invariants fail.
limitations: One real post-repair boundary proves recovery from this incident but not indefinite process reliability.
The observer source is technically restored; this does not establish profitable SP500 or SPCX expectancy.
The active live backend remains on its existing run and was not restarted.
Future process absence still requires external session/freshness monitoring.
